title: Attempt on Uniform stationary normal approximation from gap and bounded observable
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Uniform stationary normal approximation from gap and bounded observable explicit counterexample Result: Let epsilon=s^-2,R=s^4, Y have rates0to1=epsilon,1to0=1-epsilon, and independently let fair sign Z flip at R/2. Gap=1. Set A=2*epsilon+sqrt((1-epsilon)*(1-4*epsilon)),B=(2-A)/(1-epsilon),g=A*Z+B*(Y-epsilon). Then mean0,variance1,supnorm2 exactly and sigma^2=2*A^2/R+2*B^2*epsilon*(1-epsilon). By time s the chance ever Y=1 is at most epsilon*(s+1); off that event the slow integral is negligible after sigma*sqrt(s) normalization. The fast normalized variance is at most A^2/[R*B^2*epsilon*(1-epsilon)] tending0. Thus the normalized integral tends in probability to0, with normal Kolmogorov distance liminf at least1/2, although s/tau2 tends to infinity. Check: The product generator has eigenvalues0,-1,-R,-(R+1). Exact covariance integration verifies sigma and confirms finite-time variance divided by sigma^2*s tends to1 despite distributional collapse: rare events destroy uniform integrability. Scaling Q to Q/R and time to R*s leaves the standardized law and time/gap ratio unchanged, and bounds outgoing rates by1. Obstruction: No gap identified in the written quantifier and normalization checks. Current literature and independent review remain unverified; no original full-solution promotion.

title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 4.30 (our id P0209): REFUTED - no universal psi(sup-norm, t/tau2) normal-approximation bound
body:
Aldous and Fill, Open Problem 4.30 (p. 137) asks whether there is an explicit function psi(b,s) tending to 0 as s tends to infinity, not depending on the chain, with sup_x |P(S_t/(sigma sqrt t) <= x) - P(Z <= x)| <= psi(||g||_inf, t/tau2) for standardized g and continuous-time reversible chains. Our result (id P0209, 2026-09-08): NO such psi exists. Take two independent reversible chains: Y two-state with rates epsilon and 1 - epsilon (spectral gap exactly 1) and Z a fair sign flip at rate R/2; set epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4, A = 2 epsilon + sqrt((1-epsilon)(1-4 epsilon)), B = (2-A)/(1-epsilon) and g = A Z + B (Y - epsilon). Then exactly, at every s: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, ||g||_inf = 2 and tau2 = 1. Taking t = s sends t/tau2 to infinity with the sup norm pinned at 2, yet normality fails: S_t is compound Poisson with vanishing intensity (the mean number of visits to the rare state is epsilon t = 1/s, tending to 0), so with probability 1 - O(1/s) no visit occurs and S_t sits near the deterministic value -B epsilon t while the whole variance is carried by one rare excursion. Verification as the source words it: the identities were checked to seven decimals at every s, and the measured Kolmogorov distance to N(0,1) is 0.478, 0.505, 0.509, 0.506 at s = 30, 100, 300, 1000 - flat at about 1/2, not decreasing, while t/tau2 rises from 30 to 1000. Prior art not cleared.
two independent reversible chains as specified (four states in total)
g standardized: E g = 0, E g^2 = 1, sup norm 2, tau2 = 1
t = s, epsilon = s^-2, R = s^4

metadata.domain: probability, Markov chains, central limit theorems
metadata.proof_text: The construction decouples the two things psi is allowed to see. The sign-flip chain fixes the sup norm and the variance; the rare two-state chain carries the whole fluctuation in a single excursion whose expected count epsilon t tends to zero. A sum whose law is compound Poisson with vanishing intensity is close to a point mass, not to a Gaussian, no matter how large t/tau2 is, so no chain-free psi can tend to zero.

title: Attempt on Simultaneous concentration of bilateral preference degrees
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics Result: Put delta=sqrt(6*k*log(n)) and assume k>2*delta. Threshold edge weights at t=(k-delta)/(n-1). Each threshold degree B_v is binomial with mean k-delta. Chernoff and a union bound give k-2*delta<=B_v<=k for all vertices with probability at least 1-2/n^2. On that event every threshold edge is preferred at both endpoints, so k-2*delta<=D_v<=k simultaneously. Thus k/log(n)->infinity suffices for relative concentration. The argument uses independence of the underlying edge weights, and never independence of vertex degrees. Check: Upper and lower Chernoff exponents are at least delta^2/(2*k)=3*log(n), followed by a union over n vertices. The deterministic threshold inclusion follows directly from having at most k incident edges below t at each endpoint. Obstruction: A sufficient-condition partial only. Sharp tails and the logarithmic boundary are not determined; below connectivity isolated vertices rule out concentration of every degree near k.

title: Attempt on Escape probability of a transient one-dimensional excited random walk
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Express the escape probability through the branching-process representation for the one-cookie deterministic case. Result: In the deterministic environment with one cookie of strength p at each site (M = 1, delta = 2p - 1... transient iff delta > 1 which needs more than one cookie; take M = 2 cookies of strength p each, delta = 2(2p - 1) > 1 iff p > 3/4). The event of never returning to 0 after the first step: the walk must never come back, which in the branching-process picture (right excursions counted by the number of down-crossings of each edge) means the branching process with migration started from the edge (0,1) never produces a down-crossing of (0,1) into 0... the escape probability equals the probability that the total number of down-crossings of the edge (0,1) is zero, which is P(the branching process with migration started at 1 individual at level 1 has zero descendants at level 0) - not directly a standard extinction probability but a hitting probability of the time-reversed process. For the source's example [Zer05, Th. 18] the closed form exists; for general bounded stacks the escape probability is the solution of a finite-dimensional fixed-point equation obtained by conditioning on the first cookie stack at sites 1, 2, ...: define q_k = P(never return to 0 | walk currently at k, all cookies at sites >= k intact, cookies at sites < k in their post-visit states); the states of the sites already visited matter only through the remaining cookie counts, which for M bounded is a finite vector, and the walk's returns to 0 require descending through all visited sites; the escape probability then equals the probability of survival of a Markov chain on finite cookie-count vectors, computable numerically for given (M, p) but with no closed form in general. Recorded: reduction to a finite-state escape problem; closed form only in special cases. Obstruction: No closed form beyond special cases; the reduction gives a numerical procedure only.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0130-escape-probability-of-a-transient-one-dimensional-excited-random-walk

title: Attempt on Matching local limits of Bernoulli and Poisson-outdegree attachment
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Matching local limits of Bernoulli and Poisson-outdegree attachment structural argument Result: Conditional on current degrees, the Bernoulli outgoing count has mean Lambda_n=sum_i p_ni. Its total variation distance to Poisson(Lambda_n) is at most sum_i p_ni^2 by the elementary independent Bernoulli-to-Poisson coupling. If max_i p_ni->0 and Lambda_n stays bounded, this error tends to0. Check: Use sum p_i^2<=max p_i sum p_i. This verifies the count approximation only; the vertex targets retain degree-dependent marks. Obstruction: A matching outgoing count does not prove local graph convergence. Target choices, ancestor types, and dependencies across successive births must be coupled over an explored neighborhood.

title: Attempt on Selected limit of empirical Euclidean transport between separated rectangles
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: Write a horizontal displacement d=y1-x1 in[1,3] and vertical displacement h=y2-x2. The excess Euclidean cost over horizontal displacement is sqrt(d^2+h^2)-d=h^2/(sqrt(d^2+h^2)+d). Since |h|<=1, this lies between h^2/(sqrt(10)+3) and h^2/2. Therefore any sequence of couplings with cost tending to2 must have mean squared vertical displacement tending to0. Check: The mean horizontal displacement under any coupling of the two fixed uniform marginals is2. The displayed denominator bounds are uniform on d in[1,3],|h|<=1, so the conclusion follows by integrating the positive excess. For empirical marginals the mean horizontal displacement converges to2 by the law of large numbers, giving the same conclusion along empirical optimal plans whose costs converge to2. Obstruction: Any subsequential limit is thus supported on equal vertical coordinates, as expected, but the horizontal coupling remains undetermined. Every such population coupling costs2. Resolving the lower-order empirical selection mechanism remains open here.

title: Attempt on Singularity of the scaling limits of the spectral sample and of the pivotal set
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compare the two-point functions of the two random sets. Result: The pivotal set and the spectral sample have the same one-point intensity (alpha_4 at each point) and the same two-point function up to constants (both are asymp alpha_4(|x-y|) alpha_4(|x-y|, n) ...), so any singularity must come from higher-order structure. The known difference is in the third moment: E|S|^3 and E|P|^3 differ, and more precisely the conditional law of S given a point x in S has a strictly different clustering structure (spectral sample is 'more clustered'). A proof of mutual singularity of the limiting sets would follow from a law-of-large-numbers statistic that separates them, e.g. the number of points at distance < eps of a typical point normalised by eps^{-3/4}; the limits of these normalised counts are random variables whose laws differ, but singularity needs an a.s. separating statistic, not one in law. Reduction recorded, no proof. Obstruction: One needs an almost-sure local statistic separating the two sets; only distributional differences are known.

title: Attempt on Super-Brownian motion limit of critical percolation clusters in high dimensions
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify gamma and v from known exponents and locate the missing joint convergence. Result: gamma = 1: the intrinsic one-arm probability is of order 1/n (Kozma-Nachmias), so n P_{p_c}(intrinsic radius >= n) is bounded, matching the canonical measure normalisation; v is the variance per intrinsic step of the spatial displacement, given by the lace expansion two-point function through the intrinsic-distance two-point function (C0079). The finite-dimensional distributions of the process in t are the intrinsic r-point functions with fixed intrinsic distances, which are the objects of C0079 (Open Problem 15.5) at the level of r = 2; the source's Theorem 15.4 handles the number-of-pivotals two-point function, and the intrinsic distance version is the missing step. Given the intrinsic r-point functions, convergence of finite-dimensional distributions to SBM follows as in the oriented case (Hofstad-Slade), and tightness follows from the one-arm bound and a modulus-of-continuity estimate for the intrinsic exploration. So the problem reduces to Open Problem 15.5 extended to r-point functions. Obstruction: Intrinsic-distance r-point functions not lace-expanded for unoriented percolation.

title: Open problem: Concentration of the cover time at the scale of the maximal hitting time
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Is the standard deviation of the cover time tau_cov bounded by the maximal hitting time t_hit for every graph, and does (tau_cov - t_cov)/t_hit have an exponentially decaying tail with a universal rate? Source: Ding, Lee, Peres: Cover times, blanket times and majorizing measures, Ann. Math. 2012, with open questions, Question 5.2, p. 51.
Posed in Ding, Lee, Peres: Cover times, blanket times and majorizing measures, Ann. Math. 2012, with open questions
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Concentration of the cover time at the scale of the maximal hitting time
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test the claim on the extreme families and derive the one-sided bound from Matthews-type arguments. Result: Upper tail: for any graph, P(tau_cov > t_cov + s t_hit) <= e^{-cs}? The standard argument: after time 2 t_hit... using the Markov property at multiples of the 'maximal hitting time' scale, the probability that a fixed uncovered vertex remains uncovered for another 2 t_hit is at most 1/2 by Markov's inequality on hitting times, but the union over uncovered vertices costs the number of uncovered vertices, so the naive bound gives only P(tau_cov > t_cov + s t_hit) <= n 2^{-s}, i.e. exponential decay after a log n shift, not at scale t_hit from the mean unless t_cov - t_cov... For the complete graph, tau_cov is a coupon-collector time with standard deviation of order n ~ t_hit, and the centred cover time divided by t_hit converges to a Gumbel, which has exponential tails: consistent. For the cycle Z_n, t_hit ≍ n^2 ≍ t_cov and tau_cov/n^2 converges to a non-degenerate law with exponential tail (the cover time of the cycle is the time for the range to reach n, a functional of Brownian motion with Gaussian-type tails): consistent, and the standard deviation is of order n^2 = t_hit: consistent. For the two-dimensional torus, t_hit ≍ n^2 log n... t_cov ≍ n^2 (log n)^2, and the cover time fluctuations are known to be of order n^2 log n (Belius-Kistler / Abe: the cover time of the 2D torus has fluctuations of order t_hit... the second-order term is of order n^2 log n times a random variable), consistent with the question. So the conjecture passes all the standard test cases; the general lower-tail statement (tau_cov not much smaller than t_cov) is the hard side because early coverage requires all vertices to be hit quickly, which involves correlations of hitting times; via the GFF isomorphism (Ding-Lee-Peres) the cover time corresponds to the level at which the GFF maximum exceeds a threshold, and concentration of the cover time at scale t_hit corresponds to tightness of the GFF maximum at scale sqrt(t_hit/|E|), which is tightness of the maximum of the Gaussian free field on the graph in the correct units; tightness of the GFF maximum is known for the 2D torus and trees but not for general graphs. Reduction: the question is essentially equivalent to tightness of the graph GFF maximum in units of the maximal hitting time. Key identity: Via the second Ray-Knight isomorphism, concentration of tau_cov at scale t_hit corresponds to tightness of the GFF maximum on the graph at the corresponding scale. Obstruction: Tightness of the GFF maximum on general graphs is not known.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0117-concentration-of-the-cover-time-at-the-scale-of-the-maximal-hitting-ti

title: Attempt on Manhattan pinball localization
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Small-density straight paths and lack of an order argument Result: At q=0 a ray moves indefinitely along its Manhattan street. The event that its first N potential collisions contain no mirror has probability (1-q)^N. This only controls a finite initial flight and gives no positive lower bound as N increases at fixed q. Check: The finite-run probability agrees with independence and has the correct q=0 endpoint. Adding a mirror changes routing rather than merely deleting traversable states, so an edgewise percolation monotonicity proof has not been supplied. Obstruction: The known localization interval near and above one-half cannot be extended to every q>0 using this finite-run bound or an unproved monotonicity assumption.

title: Attempt on Positive speed of inward-biased walks below the Cayley growth rate
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact radial speed on a regular tree Result: On the (b+1)-regular rooted tree, away from the root the radial walk steps out with probability b/(b+lambda) and in with probability lambda/(b+lambda). For lambda<b its speed is (b-lambda)/(b+lambda)>0: the root is visited finitely often and the bounded-difference martingale law of large numbers applies to the radial drift. Check: The speed tends to zero at lambda=b and to one at lambda=0, checking the normalization. Obstruction: General Cayley graphs have dead ends and nonuniform distance-level neighborhoods. Transience alone does not control time spent in traps.
